title: Wasmtime Sandbox Escape Flaws Patched in Cranelift
content_md: Two critical Wasmtime sandbox escape flaws, CVE-2026-115889 and CVE-2026-115893, let a crafted WebAssembly (Wasm) module push the Cranelift compiler into generating unsafe machine code. The Bytecode Alliance fixed both on October 19, 2026, and rated each 9.9 under CVSS v3.1. Platforms that compile Wasm from customers or other outside parties carry the most risk, because they depend on Wasmtime to keep that code contained. One flaw affects every architecture, while the other hits ARM64 (aarch64) hosts running default settings. No exploitation has been reported, and neither advisory offers a workaround, so upgrading is the only real fix. Two Compiler Bugs Behind the Wasmtime Sandbox Escape Wasmtime is the Bytecode Alliance’s WebAssembly runtime, and Cranelift is the default compiler it uses to turn Wasm bytecode into native machine code. Isolation depends on that generated code doing exactly what the Wasm allows, so a compiler mistake can break the sandbox even when the rest of the runtime works correctly. Both flaws follow that pattern, though they fail in different places. The comparison below shows how they differ.
